data.raw_text:
REPORTED FLOODING

Flooding was reported along several portions of EDSA on Friday afternoon, with gutter-deep waters observed but still passable to all types of vehicles.

As of 3:16 p.m., the MMDA reported flooding in Mandaluyong at EDSA Ortigas Service Road southbound, EDSA Highway 54 Mall southbound, and the EDSA Shaw Tunnel northbound.

In Quezon City, gutter-deep flooding was also seen at EDSA Main Avenue northbound. The MMDA said all affected areas remained passable despite the 8-inch-deep waters, based on Metrobase CCTV monitoring.

📸 MMDA via X

data.raw_text:
INGAT PO TAYO!

Motorists were urged to take extra caution on Friday afternoon as several areas in Metro Manila reported flooding following heavy rains, according to the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA).

As of 3:59 p.m., the MMDA listed the following affected roads:
📍 Mandaluyong: EDSA Ortigas Service Rd. SB, Highway 54 Mall SB, Shaw Tunnel NB — Gutter deep (8") — Passable to all vehicles
📍 Quezon City: Multiple spots along EDSA and Commonwealth, with knee-deep floods (19") reported along Quezon Ave.-Biak na Bato — Not passable to light vehicles
📍 Makati: EDSA Guadalupe Bridge NB — Gutter deep
📍 Taguig: C5 Kalayaan Service Rd. SB — Gutter deep

The MMDA said monitoring operations are ongoing, with traffic and disaster response teams on alert. Motorists are advised to expect delays and consider alternate routes where necessary.

MAULANG BIYERNES! ☔️

PAGASA has issued a Yellow Heavy Rainfall Warning as of 4:30 p.m., Friday, June 6, over Metro Manila, Cavite, Bulacan, Bataan, Pampanga, Batangas, Laguna, Quezon, Rizal, Zambales, and parts of Tarlac, due to the combined effects of the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) and a Low Pressure Area (LPA).

⚠️ Possible flooding in flood-prone areas.

🌧️ Light to moderate, occasionally heavy rains also expected in parts of Nueva Ecija, Tarlac, and Zambales.

Authorities urge the public and local disaster management offices to closely monitor updates.
